chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who made an oath of abstention (ila') from his wife but had not yet consummated the marriage with her. He said, 'There is no ila' until he consummates the marriage with her.' Then he was asked, 'What do you think if a man swore that he would not cohabit with his wife for two years or more than that? Would that be considered ila'?'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (often referring to Imam Ali or used generally for Imams)
key_terms.إِيلاَء: Oath of abstention from sexual relations by a husband

ai.seo_question: When does the legal ruling of Ila' (oath of abstention) take effect in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the specific legal ruling of 'ila' (oath of abstention) applies only after consummation, distinguishing it from a general vow of non-cohabitation made prior to that point. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining whether the four-month waiting period for divorce or reconciliation begins, ensuring that pre-consummation vows do not trigger the same legal consequences as the Quranic 'ila'.
